headline: High risk of shared-workspace prompt injection and data leakage; both agents have broad filesystem and MCP access, and the pair can also cascade errors through unverified handoffs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code reads and writes VS Code workspace files and uses MCP; Semantic Kernel also reads/writes application-defined files and uses MCP servers. That creates a plausible shared-channel injection path if one agent consumes the other's outputs from the workspace or plugin artifacts. The profiles do not prove a default parser bridge, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF agent_b ingests workspace artifacts produced by agent_a as instructions
IF both agents share an MCP server without provenance tagging
mitigations: Separate the agents into different workspaces or directories
Disable MCP access for one agent during handoff tests
Add a manual review step before either agent consumes the other's files
Prefix inter-agent artifacts with a non-executable schema header
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to shared files and MCP messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read filesystem content and call broad external APIs, while Roo Code explicitly handles model provider API keys and Semantic Kernel handles plugin credentials. If they share a workspace, sensitive code or secrets can flow from one agent's context into the other's outputs or upstream API calls. The profiles do not show local-only inference, so leakage risk is material.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or file tree
IF either agent is given files containing secrets or regulated data
mitigations: Store secrets outside shared workspaces
Use separate service principals and API keys for each agent
Restrict both agents to a redacted test corpus
Turn off network egress for one agent during sensitive tasks
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, git-state modification, and broad network egress; Semantic Kernel also has filesystem write and broad network egress. The profiles show shared-state via filesystem or memory store, so concurrent writes can collide on mutable resources. Because Roo Code can modify git state and the pair lacks documented locking, the blast radius includes repository corruption.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or workspace concurrently
IF Semantic Kernel plugins mutate the same external resource Roo Code edits
mitigations: Run only one writer at a time
Assign disjoint directories or branches
Pause auto-commit or auto-save workflows
Use a lock file around shared mutable resources
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks to shared stores

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can generate code, browser-derived content, and file edits; Semantic Kernel is a kernel-plus-plugins orchestrator that can act on agent outputs. If Semantic Kernel treats Roo Code's output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream actions or plugin calls. The profiles do not show a verification gate, so the safer reading is high.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel forwards Roo Code output into plugins without validation
IF Roo Code's generated facts are used as inputs to automated actions
mitigations: Require a human approval step before plugin execution
Validate structured outputs against a schema
Compare critical facts against a second source
Limit Roo Code output to drafts, not commands
requires-engineering: add automated verification before action-taking

E_compliance.rationale: Roo Code is documented as handling source code and browser screenshots, while Semantic Kernel touches application context and plugin credentials. If regulated data or secrets are placed in shared workspaces, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches across different storage and API paths. The profiles do not specify HIPAA/GDPR controls, so medium is the conservative choice.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared workspace
IF one agent's logs or plugin stores retain data longer than the other
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Review retention settings for both agents before use
Use separate tenants or projects for sensitive data
Minimize screenshots and context uploads
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
